steps: Topic sentence: a best friend has several important qualities.
Supporting points with examples: loyalty; honesty; being a good listener who keeps secrets; generosity; encouraging you to improve; accepting and forgiving.
Concluding sentence: sums up the qualities that make a friend the best.

explanation_steps: Choose ONE topic. Topic 1 is a process/‘how’ paragraph written in the first person: the steps or habits you follow to protect yourself AND your friends. Topic 2 is a descriptive (expository) paragraph listing and explaining the qualities of a best friend.
Plan: topic sentence (main idea) → 3–5 supporting points, each with an example or reason → concluding sentence.
Topic 1 linkers: first of all, secondly, in addition, moreover, also, finally, because, so that. Use the present simple for habits (I wash, I wear, I remind).
Topic 2 linkers: the first/most important quality is, secondly, in addition, another quality is, moreover, finally, in short. Give an example for each quality.
Keep to about 200 words, one paragraph, and check grammar, spelling and punctuation at the end.
marking_points: Content (8): relevant topic sentence and 3–4 developed supporting points; comparison topics must compare (similarities and differences), not just describe.
Organization (6): topic sentence, logically ordered supporting sentences with transitions, a concluding sentence; ONE paragraph; unity (no irrelevant sentences).
Language (6): grammar (tenses, agreement, articles, comparatives), vocabulary, spelling and punctuation.
Length: about 200 words; clearly shorter paragraphs lose content marks.

descriptors: 7–8: clear topic sentence; 3–4 well-developed, relevant supporting points with examples or explanations; for comparison topics real similarities AND differences; about 200 words.
5–6: relevant with some support, but one point is thin or repeated.
3–4: few ideas, little support, partly off topic, or clearly too short (under about 120 words).
5–6: topic sentence → ordered supporting sentences → concluding sentence; one main idea only; smooth transitions (first of all, moreover, however, whereas, in conclusion).
3–4: logical overall, but weak or missing concluding sentence, few or repeated linkers, or one sentence off the main idea.
1–2: ideas in random order; no clear topic sentence; written as a list or several paragraphs.
5–6: accurate tenses, agreement and articles; varied sentence types; suitable vocabulary (comparatives and contrast words for comparison topics); correct spelling, capitals and punctuation.
3–4: several errors that do not block meaning; limited sentence variety or vocabulary.
1–2: frequent errors that sometimes block meaning.
0: errors make the paragraph impossible to follow.

planning_template: Topic chosen: ______ (write about ONE topic only; one paragraph of about 200 words).
Supporting point 1 + example/explanation (Topic 1: washing hands / Topic 2: loyalty): ______
Supporting point 2 + example/explanation (Topic 1: wearing a mask / Topic 2: honesty): ______
Supporting point 3 + example/explanation (Topic 1: keeping distance, covering coughs / Topic 2: a good listener): ______
Supporting point 4 + example/explanation (Topic 1: helping and advising friends / Topic 2: generosity and encouragement): ______
Linking words to use: first of all, secondly, moreover, in addition, however, on the other hand, whereas, while, finally
Concluding sentence (restate the main idea / give a final comparison or advice): ______
Check (5 minutes): one paragraph, first line indented; tenses, agreement, articles, spelling, capital letters, full stops; about 200 words.
tips: Topic 1 says ‘myself AND my friends’ – include at least one sentence about how you help or advise your friends, not only what you do alone.
Topic 2 is about QUALITIES (loyal, honest, patient …), not a story about one friend; if you describe your own friend, use him/her only as an example of each quality.

similar_questions.stem: Write a paragraph of about 200 words on how you prepare for the national examination.
similar_questions.answer: Model: Preparing for the national examination needs a clear plan and good habits. First of all, I make a timetable at the beginning of the year and give every subject a fixed time each week, so that I do not forget any subject. Secondly, I revise each lesson on the same day that I learn it and write short notes with the main points, formulas and new words. In addition, I practise with past examination papers. They show me the type of questions that are asked and help me to manage my time, and I check my answers carefully to learn from my mistakes. Moreover, I study with two classmates twice a week; we explain difficult topics to each other and test each other with questions. I also ask my teachers when I do not understand something instead of waiting until the last month. Finally, I take care of my health: I sleep at least seven hours, eat regular meals and walk in the evening to relax. In conclusion, careful planning, regular practice, cooperation with friends and a healthy life are the keys to good preparation for the national examination.
explanation_steps: Topic sentence states the main idea (a plan and good habits).
Each supporting sentence gives one step with a reason or example, joined by linkers.
The concluding sentence sums up the steps.
